ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a metal ring of mass m is suspended by a string. Half of the metal ring is in a uniform magnetic field that is horizontal and perpendicular to the plane of the ring. Starting from a certain moment, the magnetic induction intensity decreases uniformly. Then during the process in which the magnetic induction intensity decreases uniformly, which of the following statements about the magnitude of the tension in the string is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: Greater than the ring's weight mg, and gradually decreases

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a metal ring of mass m is suspended by a string. Half of the metal ring is in a uniform magnetic field that is horizontal and perpendicular to the plane of the ring. Starting from a certain moment, the magnetic induction intensity decreases uniformly. During the process in which the magnetic induction intensity decreases uniformly, compared with the ring's weight mg, is the tension in the string greater than, equal to, or less than it?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Greater than the ring's weight mg
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the metal ring is suspended by a vertical thin string from above, and the plane of the ring is in the plane of the paper. The lower-half region of the ring is drawn with “×” marks, indicating that there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper and directed inward in this region; the upper half of the ring has no magnetic-field symbols. A dashed line passes roughly horizontally through the middle of the metal ring, indicating that only the lower half of the metal ring is in the magnetic field. Reasoning: The problem says that the magnetic induction intensity decreases uniformly, so the inward magnetic flux passing through the metal ring decreases. According to Lenz's law, the induced current must hinder this decrease, and should produce an inward induced magnetic field. Therefore, viewed from the front of the figure, the direction of the induced current in the metal ring is clockwise. Looking only at the lower semicircular ring that is in the magnetic field, the clockwise current on the lower semicircle flows from the right end through the bottom to the left end. This part is subject to the Ampere force dF = I dℓ × B. Since the horizontal components of force at left-right symmetric positions cancel each other out, while the vertical components combine to be downward, the lower half-ring is subjected to a downward magnetic-field force. In addition to the weight mg, the metal ring also receives a downward magnetic-field force, so the upward tension of the thin string must be greater than mg.
